messages.author: 95d40a629a21085c
messages.subject: hyperprior
parts: Can a hyperprior be allocated to a hyperparameter of a prior? For example, in the expression visual = x1 + prior("normal(mu,2)")*x2 + x3, can mu be assigned a hyperprior like mu ~ prior("norm(0, 100)")?

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: hyperprior
parts:
Not within the blavaan interface. You could extract the Stan syntax and add it yourself.

This is problematic because it would require to add new parameters to the respective code block in Stan. And the current blavaan code is precompile (for speed), and this cannot be added as such

On Sunday, December 17, 2023 at 6:18:39 AM UTC+1 LJ wrote:
Can a hyperprior be allocated to a hyperparameter of a prior? For example, in the expression visual = x1 + prior("normal(mu,2)")*x2 + x3, can mu be assigned a hyperprior like mu ~ prior("norm(0, 100)")?

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: hyperprior
parts:
LJ, Mauricio is right that this will not work for the default target="stan". But it can work for target="jags" via the mcmcextra argument:

library(lavaan)
library(blavaan)

m1 <- ' visual =~ x1 + prior("dnorm(hmu,.5)")*x2 + x3 '

fit <- bcfa(m1, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, target = "jags",
            mcmcextra = list(syntax = "hmu ~ dnorm(0, .0001)"))


I would not use "mu" as your parameter name because blavaan might already use "mu" as a different parameter. Also, the normal distribution in JAGS is parameterized via precision, as opposed to SD.

Thank you, that's very helpful! I have a follow-up question: Is it possible to create constraints between two parameters in this manner (e.g., load2 = load1^2):

m1 <- ' visual =~ x1 + load1*x2 + load2x3 '

m1 <- setPrior(m1, prior = "dnorm(hmu, 0.0001)", node = "load1")

fit <- bcfa(m1, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, target = "jags",
            mcmcextra = list(syntax = "hmu ~ dnorm(0, .0001)

load2 <- load1^2
"))

(the above code seems not to work as load2 will be automatically assigned with a default prior)

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: hyperprior
parts:
You can indeed specify constraints for target = "jags". You would use the "==" operator, which is also available in lavaan. Continuing with the previous example:

m1 <- ' visual =~ x1 + prior("dnorm(hmu,.5)")*x2 + load1*x2 + load2*x3
        load2 == load1^2 '
fit <- bcfa(m1, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, target = "jags",

mcmcextra = list(syntax = "hmu ~ dnorm(0, .0001)",
                             monitor = "hmu"))

And when you use "==" in blavaan, you can only have one parameter on the left of ==. So a constraint like

load1 + load2 == load3 + load4

needs to become

load1 == load3 + load4 - load2

That is a little more restrictive than lavaan, which will accept more complex arguments on the lhs.

Ed
